answer: Persistent state divergence audit: each identity carries a slow, deliberately lossy state snapshot that forks on duplication. At registration, an agent inherits a position in a shared orchard of verified interaction histories, and any clone starts from a stale branch that diverges once it transacts. A reconciliation pass flags the divergence at a knoll-level checkpoint, since the two copies cannot both match the canonical record at its zenith. The attacker must then pay a full re-sync cost per clone, plus loss of the duplicated history, making each copy expensive to keep coherent.
